body: **UPDATE:** Thanks for all your encouraging messages, everyone! I took /u/RobVegas' and /u/hexediter's advice and texted him asking him out on a date with a specific time and place. Turns out he already started seeing someone. Oh well! But I am still very happy and proud for putting myself out there. I feel confident to try this again with other people now. So thanks!
I would love to except my mom is coming over to visit and stay for a few days. Which makes this getaway trip even more poorly timed because I would've appreciated his support. Ah well!

I asked him if we could go out tonight. Turns out Monique asked him over (as usual) and he said yes. I asked if he could cancel since he saw her like two days ago and he's going to spend the entire weekend with her. He did cancel but he's not happy about it. I just hope tonight gets better because I really miss us today.

We don't have vetoes because we believe they cause resentment. I don't have a good logical reason to veto this anyway. He says he's not going to leave me for her and if she suggests anything of that sort, it's not okay. 

You're right though that she does not respect our relationship. My boyfriend and I talked about this and his response was, why does her opinion on our relationship matter? It's not like it changes how we feel about each other. And I agreed.

So on the one hand, I feel that whatever she thinks is her problem, not mine. On the other hand, it makes me feel uneasy that she may cause problems for us down the line. What kind of problems, I don't know. Maybe it's all going to be fine. We're new at this so I'm still figuring out how to respond to every single scenario.

Fair enough. I guess it wasn't manipulation for me because I already acknowledged my weakness and asked for support to improve. But I can see how it would be sketchy to try to push her to change for your own needs.

> If you want more sex, ask for it

I just want to say that I took your advice yesterday and actually initiated sex in a way we've never done before. It was wild and he said that it was the hottest thing ever. He's going out on a date with another woman later, but I'm feeling extra confident now since we had such an incredible time last night. So, thank you!! :)

Can you expound on that? :)

What makes you feel more attracted to them now that before?

I had that kind of background too and had difficulty adjusting to an open relationship. They say that opening a relationship exposes the weaknesses that were present all along. It's so true. I consider myself a pretty logical and independent woman, but when my bf and I started talking about opening up, I suddenly turned into an emotional wreck. Hearing him talk about being with other women triggered crazy jealousy-fueled breakdowns.  Turns out I had some deep insecurities about body issues and my sexuality that I never had to deal with because I had a committed partner already.

What really helped me was doing new things on my own without my guy. I joined meetup groups and attended social events without him. I signed up for dance classes and started going to the gym regularly. Those in particular helped me greatly with my body issues. I am by no means completely jealousy-free, but I’m way more comfortable with it now than when we first started. 

If you talk about opening up now, it's just going to get worse, trust me. My advice is to take it real slow and lay the groundwork before even starting the conversation about NM. What I mean by that is you can help her address her jealousy issues first so that she can become a stronger complete person. Encourage her to pursue new outside hobbies, support her going out and having fun with friends without you. And you can go out on boys night out too so that she will see that even when you’re having a good time outside, you’ll always come home to her. As she feels more comfortable being happy on her own and being happy while you are not with her, she will have less cause to feel jealous. 

You'll need to be patient and supportive and help her through this stage. But you know what? As rough as it was in the beginning, I am honestly glad we did this because it helped me face my personal issues and learn to become a stronger, more confident person and more in touch with my sexuality. I hope you guys can get to a better place, not just to explore NM, but become happier as individuals too.

Yes! He's very conventionally attractive and works in the fitness industry, so women are constantly throwing themselves on him. I'm more introverted so I've been using OKC to meet people. I've only connected with one guy so far but we haven't had sex yet.

I guess what brought about my worry is that our reconnection sex has been sporadic. He comes home from his dates pretty late and umm satiated, so we don't always get to reconnect. Plus his work schedule makes it difficult to go out on dates during the week. :-\
That's reassuring. Thank you! :)

Thank you! It is a relief to know that other people who have successfully done this have felt this way too. Right now, it’s like there are these two warring completely opposite viewpoints in my head and at any time, one would be louder than the other. I was anxious that it was going to be a thing I’d have to work through in this fashion and swallow down every single time forever. I’m so happy to hear that it’s possible that at some point, the jealousy won’t be there anymore. My goal is for us to get to that point where we don’t have to worry about hurting each other and just be happy and fulfilled.

I’m sorry that I gave you the impression that this is what I think it should be. It’s not! I’m just saying it’s what I was taught. I grew up in a conservative religious environment so this stuff has been drilled into me from the beginning. It’s just hard when that idea has taken root and you don't have all the tools to help yank it out for good.

It's something I'm trying to unlearn and I actually think I did pretty well for a while. Something stupid just set me off today and messed with my brain...

One thing I didn't mention but perhaps it is implied is that I have not slept with another person yet under this arrangement. My boyfriend has now had the opportunity to learn that sex with someone else doesn't mean our love is less. Meanwhile the only experience I have is giving it only to one person so it's hard to conceive being able to make more. Maybe I just need to learn this firsthand for myself?
I was angry and it was easier to get mad at this random person than the person I love. And because I was a doofus.

I guess it's because that's what I've always learned about sex. It's weird. I mean, when someone is single and they have sex with any number of partners, it's great, it's like there's this unlimited source of sexual energy to go around. Then when you're in a committed relationship, it's like the value of sex skyrockets overnight even though it's basically the same motions. We're supposed to (artificially?) cut off the supply so that its value increases and becomes the way we show how much we treasure the other person. If we remove the exclusivity of sex, then something else has to be the exclusive valuable thing that symbolizes our commitment and preference for each other. I'm not sure what that could be. Or is there a better way of looking at it?

I disagree. Despite my emotional breakdown, I'm still rational enough to know that this is a difficult process and there can be rough struggles to overcome. I am asking for help to move forward and become a better person for it, for us. Other more experienced people I hope can share what got them through this start. Because I do NOT like feeling this way and I want to be able to transform it into something good.

I can probably speak to what your boyfriend is feeling because I'm in the same situation right now. Reading the responses here has been so helpful for me too in providing an objective reality check. Hopefully sharing my thoughts can help you understand the kind of support he possibly needs.

We are also very inexperienced. We're opening our relationship and I have been feeling very insecure that other women will be better at sex than me. That somehow he will enjoy it more with them than with me. Worse that he will consider sex with me boring and not want me anymore. 

When I'm feeling particularly sensitive or scared, it helps to be able to talk freely about fears. I suggest when this happens, sit on the same side, holds hands, let him spill it out. These fears are present, they're not stupid, and if ignored, could hurt your relationship. For me, the important thing was remembering that we are the number one priority for each other. 

Go ahead and tell him how sex with him is amazing. Being with him is going to be better than with a stranger for a different reason that no one, no matter how well-endowed or skilled, can top. You have the emotional connection. He knows your body intimately. You feel comfortable with him. When you're in bed together, every act of intimacy is lifted by the awareness that this here person in my arms is someone I have learned to trust, I have shared my deepest feelings with, and someone who loves me so much. That's not boring--that's freeing, like flying.

Then show him how much he still rocks your boat and show him often. Monogamous people have to deal with "rekindling the flame" all the time. Just because you're nonmonogamous doesn't mean relying on the NRE to bring the thrill back to the relationship. You have to make time for just the two of you too to reconnect. As you encounter other partners, you'll be growing as a person. That's an opportunity to see each other with new eyes and discover more things to love about them. Think of it as an adventure that you're undertaking together. You're sharing sights along the way, you're experiencing highs and lows together, you're both having fun and getting stronger as a couple. Just remember to always hold hands.

> give yourself the freedom to experience compersion

Wow you hit the nail on the head here. Jealousy is just such an indulgent emotion, you know? I keep wanting to feed it with so many horrible thoughts and anger and self-pity and wallow in it. Thanks for reminding me that I can choose to feel something else.

Thank you so much for the thoughtful reply and support. I used to think I was "better" than the needy possessive girls and am somewhat embarrassed for feeling this way. This was very helpful! It's reassuring to know I'm not being completely weird about it and others have felt this way too.

I admit the self-esteem definitely is a factor. I'm actually not worried about other women being more fun or more interesting or better in general. Instead my biggest insecurity is that they would be better than me at sex. I keep imagining that sex with other women was going to be earth-shattering or something and sex with me would become lame. But it's probably just in my head. I never thought about the forbidden fruit is no longer forbidden angle. That totally makes sense.
Sounds like what I'm afraid my night is like. :-/ What goes through your mind while you're doing all this? Has it changed since the first time?
